producer_report.summary: Added the drain in-flight table (build job 3). The run now reports its own stages: `Athena::go_with_stages` tells a `StageSink` when it enters the producer, the checks, the verifier and the landing. `Athena::go` passes a no-op sink. The producer is reported at the top of every producer-loop pass, so a self-check send-back reports producer again. Checks are reported only when they actually run, and a resumed job goes straight to the verifier. The worktree comes from one new helper, `StateDir::work_dir` (`jobs/<id>/work`), which `producer_snapshot` also uses, so the row cannot name the kept-work directory. The real drain steps write `in-flight.json` in the state directory: job, stage and worktree rows, written atomically under one lock. A rejected job's row waits for its retry, which moves it to the new job and keeps its stage, and the retry's producer then sets it to producer. The row is removed when the item's work ends and after a landing. The drain reads the file at its start and notes leftover rows without acting on them. A missing file is empty. A file that cannot be read is moved to `in-flight.json.corrupt`, noted, and the drain continues. A failed write is a warning line, never a job failure. The new `Steps::in_flight` and `Steps::item_over` have default bodies, so existing steps and the `max_in_flight = 1` behavior are unchanged. Root cause of both rejected attempts: the stage was inferred outside the pipeline (display text) and the path was built in two places. Both now come from the pipeline and a single helper. Tests: six new integration tests through `drain::drain` over `RealSteps`, six unit tests for the table, one lifecycle test with a recording sink and one `state.rs` test for the helper and stage names. CHANGELOG.md and async-drain.md sections 7 and 12 are updated.

criteria_check.evidence: Two tests in tests/drain.rs through drain::drain over RealSteps. in_flight_row_goes_producer_checks_verifier_and_is_producer_again_after_a_self_check_send_back: the table reads producer, producer, checks, verifier. in_flight_row_moves_from_verifier_back_to_producer_when_the_rejected_job_is_retried: the row reads verifier while the retry is read, then belongs to the retry job at verifier at dispatch, then reads producer with the retry's work tree during the second producer invocation, with one row throughout. Note: Athena::go never re-enters the producer from checks or the verifier within one job; the return to producer after a verifier rejection happens through the drain's retry (a new job), so the row is moved across the retry, as the accepted plan says. The lifecycle test stage_report_names_the_producer_again... asserts the sink sequence producer, producer, checks, verifier.

open_issues: Departure from the plan's wording: producer_snapshot lost its unused job_dir parameter and now builds the path from state.work_dir(ctx.id()).
`dispatch` takes a small `Outputs { ui, stages }` struct instead of two arguments, to satisfy clippy's argument limit.
The row keeps the producer's work path at checks and verifier, though mod.rs removes that directory after the candidate is built. A recovery job may want the verify directory for those stages.
A corrupt file found mid-run by a table write (not at drain start) is moved aside silently. Only the drain-start read produces a note.
A leftover row for an interrupted job that the drain then retries is taken over by the retry (bookkeeping only). Nothing recovers a leftover row.
The 'checks' and 'dispatched' observations in the new drain tests use Ui progress lines as triggers only. The assertions are on the table file.
mistakes: My first edit of RealSteps::land left a fragment of the old body behind and broke the file. I noticed it on reading back and fixed it before compiling.
I first expected two reader starts in the retry test. A third comes from introspection, which I found from the failing run and corrected in the test.
learnings: Athena::go never re-enters the producer from checks or the verifier within one job. The only in-job producer re-entry is the self-check send-back. After a verifier rejection the return to producer is the drain's retry, a new job.
In tests, Role::Reader is also used by the introspection of a rejected job, so a drain over a rejected job sees three reader starts (read, introspect, retry read).
clippy's too_many_arguments (limit 7) bit `dispatch`, so ui and stages are bundled in a private `Outputs` struct.
After the candidate is built, mod.rs removes the producer's work tree before the checks. At the checks and verifier stages the row's worktree therefore names a path that no longer exists.
desires: A test seam to force a configured check to fail would let the checks-to-producer case be exercised without the verifier rejection route.
